body:
One more datapoint to inform this decision that I just remembered, about whether and how UAs use the flexibility the spec currently offers them... when `devicePixelRatio` was >1, Chrome used to pick the closest resource (by geometric mean) to the density target, rather than the smallest one that was larger. So when offered a 1.9x resource and a 3x resource when trying to hit a 2x target, Chrome would pick the 1.9x, while Safari and Firefox would pick the 3x.

[I just tested and this no longer seems to be the case](https://codepen.io/editor/eeeps/pen/01a13b44-dda6-728c-b0dd-b120a6758594), but I'm pretty sure it was the last time I looked, in 2024.

When did this change, and why? Presumably interop?

>     [I just tested and this no longer seems to be the case](https://codepen.io/editor/eeeps/pen/01a13b44-dda6-728c-b0dd-b120a6758594), but I'm pretty sure it was the last time I looked, in 2024.
>     When did this change, and why? Presumably interop?

This would be https://github.com/chromium/chromium/commit/c1e91d248c.
Yea, the ratio of complexity cost vs. measurable value *for browsers* to maintain this kind of divergence wasn't worth it.
